editorial:
Imagine two families who have been best friends for years and are desperate to merge their bloodlines through a marriage. You get Eesho and Anna, two young people who seem like a perfect match on paper but can't stand each other in person. The whole thing feels like a classic family comedy at first, with parents pushing their kids together while the kids roll their eyes. It has a warm, cozy vibe that makes you feel like you are sitting right there in the living room with them, watching all the chaos unfold in a beautiful setting.

What really makes this work is the acting and the way the story flips on its head. You think you know exactly where it is going, but the movie throws a few curveballs that keep you interested. The pacing is snappy, though some might find the family drama a bit repetitive.
endingExplained: The big twist is that Eesho and Anna were already secretly dating and had a child together before the parents tried to set them up. They pretended to hate each other to hide the truth and avoid a family scandal. In the end, the parents find out the secret, but they accept the situation because of their love for their grandkids. The movie wraps up with the two families staying close and everyone finally being honest with each other.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves cozy family stories and unexpected secrets.
